why: no model has been rendered and compared with the unit
claim: The filter a stereo flanger puts in front of itself and the filter a stereo chorus puts in front of itself are one section. Swept at every setting the chorus's was published at -- 15 of them across the two filter shapes the byte beside it offers -- the two types return the same skirt over a hundred and thirteen twelfth-octave bands to a median of 0.08 dB at worst, where those runs repeat themselves to 0.08 dB and where one step of the byte being swept moves the profile by at least 0.15 dB. The agreement is at the floor and the thing it is being told from is two to ten times the floor, so this is the reading saying the same section twice and not the reading running out. The page prints the two types' parameter lists identically -- same order, same addresses, same ranges -- with one entry in the flanger's that the chorus has not got, a feedback level in the slot the chorus leaves empty. That list is what made the question worth asking and it is not what answers it; what this file claims is the front end, and what the loop is around is queued.
adds: Each record says what one type's pre-filter byte does to a band profile. What is read out of the pair is that the two profiles are the same profile -- a comparison between records, made against a third figure neither record states, which is what one step of the swept byte is worth under the same reading.
refutedBy: The two pre-filters departing at a setting neither run asked -- the grid is eleven of a hundred and twenty-eight through the low pass and four through the high pass, so a table that agreed at those and not between them would look exactly like this. Or either type's filter turning out to move with something the other's does not: both runs parked the modulator and opened the loop, and a pre-filter that depended on either would have been read at one point of a surface rather than as a curve.
whatItWouldChange: Two of the sixty-four types stop being two front ends. One pre-filter section, one byte choosing between off, a low pass and a high pass, and one cutoff table, serve both -- and the cutoff table is the one the frequency class already closed.

It puts the question where it belongs. If the front ends are one section then what separates a chorus from a flanger on this unit is whatever the feedback byte reaches, and that is one run rather than a comparison of two whole types.

eraPriors.claim: A chorus and a flanger on a fixed-point part of this period are the same arithmetic: a short modulated delay summed with the dry signal, with the flanger differing by a path from the delay's output back to its input. Writing them as two stages costs two copies of the interpolator and the modulator for one extra multiply-accumulate of difference.
eraPriors.why: It says why one front end being shared is worth reading as the two types being one stage rather than as two stages that happen to filter alike. It carries none of the claim: what is claimed is the section the measurement reached.
eraPriors.wouldBeWrongIf: The two front ends had differed. They did not, at fifteen settings across two filter shapes, by more than the runs repeat themselves.

alternatives.reading: Two separate filter sections written from one specification, rather than one section reached from two types.

separatedBy.sensitivity_here: Not applicable. The two readings predict the same output at every setting of every byte, so no sensitivity would help.
separatedBy.why_not_separable: Nothing leaving this unit's sockets distinguishes one routine called from two places from two routines computing the same numbers. The archive can say the responses are the same, which it does; what it cannot say is how many times the coefficients are stored. The era prior leans one way and a prior may not close a claim.

alternatives.reading: The two types share a front end and nothing else -- the same pre-filter bolted to two different delay lines and two different modulators.

separatedBy.observable: The modulation depth of both types read as a pitch excursion at the same settings of `40 03 07` Depth and `40 03 06` Rate, with the flanger's `40 03 08` at 64 so its loop is open. A flanger with no feedback and a chorus are the same arithmetic if the delay line and the modulator are shared, so the excursion in cents either matches at every depth setting or it does not.

predicts.one stage reached twice: The same excursion at every depth setting, to the vibrato reading's own repeats.
predicts.a shared front end only: Excursions that differ at some depth setting by more than one step of the depth byte is worth.

separatedBy.divergence: One step of the depth byte, which on the types already read this way is several per cent of the excursion.
separatedBy.sensitivity_here: The vibrato stage repeats an excursion to a few parts in a thousand on the records already published with it, which is well inside one step of the byte.

run.stimulus: a held tone, rate parked low enough to resolve the sweep

alternatives.reading: The flanger's extra parameter is a loop around the same delay line the chorus uses, which is the thing the two lists being one row apart suggests and the thing nothing here has measured.

separatedBy.observable: The decay of the flanger's response at several settings of `40 03 08`, with the modulator parked so the delay is fixed. A loop around a delay of d milliseconds puts its resonances at multiples of 1/d and makes them sharper as the byte goes up; the pre-delay byte then moves those resonances by exactly what it moves the delay by, which is what says the loop is around that delay rather than around something else.

predicts.a loop around the shared delay: A comb whose spacing is one over the pre-delay setting, moving with the pre-delay byte and sharpening with the feedback byte.
predicts.a second structure of its own: Resonances that do not move with the pre-delay byte, or do not space themselves by it.

separatedBy.divergence: The whole spacing of a comb, which at a pre-delay of a few milliseconds is hundreds of hertz.
separatedBy.sensitivity_here: A twelfth-octave band set separates 0.0847 octaves, which at the frequencies a comb of this spacing puts its teeth is far finer than one tooth.

run.stimulus: the same held note, modulator parked, pre-delay asked at two values so the comb has to move
